reconcile.connective: Commentators read 70 and 75 as the same migration counted by two text traditions — the Hebrew total versus the Septuagint that Stephen followed, with extra Joseph-line descendants added.

discrepancy.connective: The objection was pressed by the Jewish polemicist Isaac of Troki, who charged that Stephen's seventy-five flatly errs against the seventy fixed in the Hebrew of Genesis, Exodus, and Deuteronomy.

skeptic.name: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki
skeptic.attribution: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki (d. 1594), Chizzuk Emunah (Faith Strengthened), pt. 2, ch. 63

excerpts.excerpt_text: In the speech of Stephen (Act 7:14) the number is stated to be seventy-five; but as that estimate includes five sons of Ephraim and Manasseh (Ch1 7:14-20), born in Egypt, the two accounts coincide.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names the 70-vs-75 gap and resolves it: the extra five (Joseph's grandsons via Ephraim/Manasseh) account for Stephen's larger figure, so 'the two accounts coincide.'

excerpts.excerpt_text: But there is no contradiction; Moses and Stephen are speaking of different things; Moses speaks of the seed of Jacob, which came out of his loins, who came into Egypt, and so excludes his sons' wives; Stephen speaks of Jacob and all his kindred, among whom his sons' wives must be reckoned, whom Joseph called to him …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explicitly denies the contradiction and supplies a distinct harmonization (different scope of 'who is counted' — Moses' loins-descendants vs Stephen's wider kindred including wives).

excerpts.excerpt_text: The number seventy-five is probably taken from the Septuagint (the Greek translation of the Old Testament) for Gen 46:27. The Septuagint includes three descendants of Ephraim and two of Manasseh at Gen 46:20, making for a total of five more persons, whereas the Hebrew text does not include descendants for Joseph's sons.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Locates the discrepancy in the textual source (Stephen follows the LXX, which adds five Joseph-line descendants) — the strongest text-critical statement of the harmonization, distinct from JFB/GILL.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Acts 7:14
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill works the 70/75 numbers line by line, answers Isaac of Troki's charge that Stephen erred, and shows the Septuagint count of seventy-five need not be a corruption.
